questions.stem:
Consider the line $L_1$ defined by the Cartesian equation $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=y=\dfrac{3-z}{1}$. (i) Show that the point $(-1, 0, 3)$ lies on $L_1$.
(ii) Find a vector equation of $L_1$.

Let $n\in\mathbb Z^+$.

Prove by mathematical induction that $5^{2n}-2^{3n}$ is divisible by $17$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z^+$.

A garden centre sells seeds for two varieties of sunflowers: large and giant. The heights of large sunflowers are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is known that $25\%$ of large sunflowers have a height of over $180\text{ cm}$.

Given that $\mu+A\sigma=180$, where $A\in\mathbb R$, find the value of $A$.

Curve $C$ satisfies $4x^2+y^2-24x+4y+20=0$. Its topmost point is $A$.

Use implicit differentiation to show $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{4(3-x)}{y+2}$.

figures.alt: Vertical ellipse centred at (3,−2), entirely right of the y-axis. A is the topmost point; the coordinate axes cross left of the ellipse.

questions.stem:
A particle moves in a straight line with velocity $v(t)=e^{-\sin t}\cos(2t)$ $\dfrac{m}{s}, 0\leqslant t\leqslant5$ seconds.

Find the maximum speed.

A small boat moves along a straight canal. Taking east as the positive direction, its velocity $t$ seconds after it passes a lock gate is $v(t)=t^3-9t$ m s$^{-1}$, for $0\le t\le 4$. For which times is the boat speeding up?

A particle moves in a straight line so that its velocity, $v$ m s$^{-1}$, at time $t$ seconds is given by $v(t)=(t-2)\mathrm e^{-t}$, for $0\le t\le 5$. Find the interval of time during which the speed of the particle is increasing. Justify your answer.

Consider the function $f(x)=2^x-\dfrac1{2^x}$, $x\in\mathbb R$. The function $g$ is given by $g(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{x^2-2x-3}$, where $x\in\mathbb R$, $x\ne-1$, $x\ne3$.

Solve the inequality $f(x)\geqslant g(x)$.

The graph of $y=f(x)$ for $-5\le x\le 5$ is shown in the following diagram.
The curve passes through the points $(-4.93,1)$, $(-4.27,-1)$ and $(0.292,-1)$. Solve the inequality $|f(x)|\ge (f(x))^2$.

figures.alt: Graph on $-5\leq x\leq5$, with a minimum near $(-2.8,-3)$, roots near $-4.6$ and $2.1$, and $y$-intercept near $-1.2$. Marked points $(-4.93,1)$, $(-4.27,-1)$ and $(0.292,-1)$.

questions.stem:
Consider the family $y=x^3+ax^2+b$, $x\in\mathbb R$, with real parameters $a\neq0$ and $b$. The stationary points are $P(0,b)$ and $Q\left(-\dfrac{2a}{3},\dfrac{4a^3}{27}+b\right)$. Take $a>0$ and $b>0$.

Find $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ and hence determine whether each point is a local maximum or minimum.
Consider a random variable $X$ such that $X\sim\mathrm B(n,0.25)$. Determine the least value of $n$ such that $\mathrm P(X\geqslant1)>0.99$.

The graph of $f$ has a local maximum $A\left(-1,-\dfrac{5}{2}\right)$, a local minimum $B\left(0,\dfrac{15}{2}\right)$, vertical asymptote $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ and oblique asymptote $y=5x+5$, as shown.

Sketch $y=\dfrac{15}{f(x)}$, clearly indicating asymptotes and axis intercepts.

figures.alt: Two branches of f, labelled extrema A and B, vertical asymptote x=−1/2 and oblique y=5x+5.

questions.stem:
The following diagram shows the graph of $y=\frac{Ax+B}{x-4}$, where $x\in\mathbb{R}$, $x\neq 4$ and $A,B\in\mathbb{Z}$.
The graph passes through the points $\mathrm{P}(-10,1)$ and $\mathrm{Q}(3,-12)$. Describe a sequence of transformations that would map the graph of $y=\frac{1}{x}$ onto the graph of $y=\frac{Ax+B}{x-4}$.

figures.alt: Rational-function graph with vertical and horizontal dashed asymptotes, passing through $\mathrm P(-10,1)$ and $\mathrm Q(3,-12)$; axes labelled $x,y$.

questions.stem:
$x^4+px^3-2x^2+qx-3$ is exactly divisible by $(x+1)^2$, with real $p,q$.

Find $p$ and $q$.

The function $f$ is defined as
$$f(x) = \frac{x^2 + ax + b}{x + 1}, \quad \text{where } x \neq -1 \text{ and } a, b \in \mathbb{Z}.$$
Now consider the case where the graph of $f$ has a vertical asymptote, an oblique asymptote with equation $y = x - 4$, and at least one point of zero gradient.
From part (c), $a=-3$.

Show that $b \geq -3$.

questions.label: 16(a)
questions.stem:
Consider the arithmetic sequence $a,p,q,\ldots$, where $a,p,q\ne0$.

Show that $2p-q=a$.

questions.label: 16(b)
questions.stem:
Consider the arithmetic sequence $a,p,q,\ldots$, where $a,p,q\ne0$. Consider the geometric sequence $a,s,t,\ldots$, where $a,s,t\ne0$.

Show that $s^2=at$.

questions.label: 16(c)
questions.stem:
Consider the arithmetic sequence $a,p,q,\ldots$, where $a,p,q\ne0$. Consider the geometric sequence $a,s,t,\ldots$, where $a,s,t\ne0$. The first term of both sequences is $a$. It is given that $q=t=1$.

Show that $p>\dfrac12$.

A farmer is growing a field of wheat plants. The height, $H\text{ cm}$, of each plant can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is known that $P(H<94.6)=0.288$ and $P(H>98.1)=0.434$.

Find the value of $\mu$ and the value of $\sigma$.

Consider the curve $C$ defined by the equation $\mathrm e^{x+y}=x^2+y^2$, shown on the following diagram. The curve has a line of symmetry $y=x$. There are two points on the curve $C$ where the tangent is horizontal. These points are labelled $P$ and $Q$.

Show that $\dfrac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\dfrac{2x-\mathrm e^{x+y}}{\mathrm e^{x+y}-2y}$.

figures.alt: Implicit curve C: e^(x+y)=x^2+y^2, symmetric about dashed line y=x. Axes x,y mark -3,0,3. A single branch extends from the upper left, curves around the origin without passing through it, and continues to the lower right. Horizontal tangencies P (left, local low point) and Q (right, local high point) are marked below the positive x-axis. The original figure does not label their coordinates.

questions.stem:
The mass, M grams, of a randomly chosen egg from a certain farm is normally distributed with mean 62 and standard deviation 8. An egg is classified as undersized if its mass is less than a grams. It is known that 5% of the eggs from the farm are undersized.

(c) Hence find the largest integer value of m for which P(M < m) < 0.05.

The random variable $X$ is normally distributed with mean $10$ and standard deviation $2$.

Find the probability that $X$ is more than $1.5$ standard deviations above the mean.

$f(x)=\dfrac{(2x+a)^3}{(x+5)^2}$, $x\neq-5$ and $a>0$.

Find $f'(x)$ in terms of $a$.
